correctness.rationale: Last-reset decomposition gives A_n=rΣ_{m<n}q^m D_m+q^n D_n. Exact logistic-doubling conjugacy x=sin²(πt), f∘h(t)=h(2t) yields D_m=2^m |sin(2^(m+1)πt)|/sin(2πt). Writing R=2q reduces rates to a weighted sum of b_m. For R<=1 a uniform upper O(n) and lower positive constant force rate zero. For R>1, first Borel–Cantelli plus exp-small measure of sine zeros yields almost-everywhere universal exponential growth rate log R (one event independent of r). Sparse zero blocks of length L_j≈αk_j with well-separated next blocks and 010 recovery create limsup=logR and a midblock upper rate ≤logR/(1+α/2)<logR for every R∈(1,2); digit-cylinder Frostman mass and covers give dim 1/(1+α) and union over α→0 and prefixes is dense null dim one. The sum estimate works because R/2<1. Independently enumerated all 2^n reset histories for n=2,3,5 at rational seed 2/7 and matched the exact renewal identity; this finite check does not establish the fractal theorem.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge after actual comparison: Aron–Kulkarni supplies the SAME renewal identity and typical chaotic rate, which the current proof explicitly credits. It does not in the accessible substantive material state a simultaneous-for-all-r dense null full-dimension irregular seed set; its typical growth derivation assumes a seed-independent chaotic Lyapunov exponent. Classical full-dimension irregular Birkhoff/Lyapunov sets concern unsmoothed orbit averages, and their existence alone does not entail nonconvergence of the positive renewal-weighted aggregate. The constructed zero-block/recovery inequalities establish an additional distinct boundary of uniform seed dependence.
residual_risks: Possible general subadditive/nonadditive thermodynamic irregular-set theorem could subsume this exact weighted-renewal special case under a reduction not inspected.
Result proves one dense null set, not exact classification of every anomalous seed or pathwise random exponents.

value.rationale: A natural exact boundary to a published chaotic resetting sensitivity prediction: typical formula fails to define a rate on a dense set of maximal Hausdorff dimension although that set is null, uniformly for every subcritical reset probability. Establishes a motivated distinction between typical and pointwise universality using explicit recoverable Cantor dimensions; not a routine isolated numeric example.

final_claim: In f(x)=4x(1-x) with Bernoulli reset to the initial interior seed, the annealed absolute seed derivative rate is zero for all seeds at reset rates r>=1/2; for every r<1/2 the almost-everywhere rate is log(2(1-r)), but one common dense null Hausdorff-dimension-one set of seeds has nonconvergent rate simultaneously for every subcritical r.
limitations: Only interior seeds and parameter-four logistic map; no classification of all exceptional seeds and no pathwise random derivative result.
Historical novelty is qualified, not a claim of exhaustive search.
